headline: Anthropic publishes detailed recommendations for designing and reporting AI safety evaluations
summary: Anthropic’s 13 November 2026 engineering post presents recommendations for designing, running and reporting AI safety evaluations. It emphasizes matching the design to the question, measuring harm-related behavior rather than refusal alone, testing multi-turn and realistic scenarios, validating graders against independent human labels, preregistering analyses, and reporting uncertainty and configuration. The post reports that appropriate-response rate in one Claude Fable 5.1 multi-turn suicide and self-harm evaluation was 60% (±14%) on the API without a system prompt and 94% (±7%) on claude.ai with the product system prompt. Anthropic’s later official system card reproduces those rates and uncertainty. These are first-party results; the comparison does not isolate one mitigation, and the review did not establish external generalization.
